title: Buying from the list without buying twice
target: How to use the buying lists in Supermarket Simulator, and how to tell what a content pack adds before you spend on its goods.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A computer or tablet in the shop
At least one pack installed if you want its goods

steps.do: Buy from the list rather than walking the shop looking for something to order.
steps.because: what can be bought is kept as sales items with a kind of sale of its own, so stock, equipment and fittings share one way of being shown (SalesItem, SalesType)

steps.do: Filter the list before you scroll it.
steps.because: the list can be filtered, with filter types and filtered items, including one for a toolbox (FilterType, FilteredItem, ToolboxItemFilterType)

steps.do: Know that a row can toggle something rather than only describe it.
steps.because: every row is a UI element of its own and there is an item that toggles a product (SalesUIElement, ProductToggleItem)

steps.do: Check what the catalogue is showing you through its own viewer.
steps.because: what the list shows goes through a product viewer (ProductViewer)

steps.do: Look at the pack screen before you buy a pack's goods.
steps.because: the game has a screen of its own for packs, with an element per pack and a controller behind it (DLCScreen, DLCScreenController, DLCElement)

steps.do: Check whether the pack is actually installed, because that decides what you can sell.
steps.because: pack information is held as its own record and a flag states whether a pack is present, with a list of the products that belong to packs and a separate list of what a pack licenses (DlcInformation, DlcInstalled_t, DLCReader, dlcProducts, dlcProductLicences)

steps.do: Expect a pack's goods to need the fixture that came with the pack.
steps.because: there is a list of the displays that come with packs (dlcDisplaysSO)

commonMistakes: Buying a pack's goods on a machine where the pack is not installed.
Scrolling the whole catalogue instead of filtering it.
Ordering a fitting twice because the row toggles rather than describes.
Expecting pack goods to sit on base-game fixtures.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
